dialog.body: Utilities billing, this is Priya. How can I help you?
Yes, good morning. This is Sheila Sullivan. I am calling about my water and sewer bill. It is wrong, I think. Much too high.
I'm sorry to hear that, Ms. Sullivan. Can you give me the service address?
Twenty-three Old Beach Road. Down by Easton's Beach. I have lived there a long time and this bill is nearly double what I pay every quarter.
Okay, let me pull that up. Has anything changed at the property recently?
Yes. That is the thing. A new meter was installed last month. A man came, he was in the basement maybe forty minutes, and he put in the new one. Then this bill comes and it is not right.
I see a meter change noted on the account. The new bill would be the first one with the new meter, so I want to look at the reading. Did you have any leaks or plumbing work around that time?

I had a plumber out, yes. Two weeks before the meter. He fixed the toilet in the upstairs bathroom, the flapper, the running one. I kept the receipt. I keep everything. It has the date and the work he did.
That's helpful. A running toilet can add a lot of usage, but if it was repaired before the meter change, it shouldn't explain the new reading. Do you have the bill in front of you?
I do. The previous reading, then the current reading, and the difference is, one moment, a very large number. I did not use that. I am one person. I wash a load of laundry on Tuesdays. That is all.

Understood. What I can do is flag the account for a meter reading verification. Someone would check the new meter and the reading that was entered at installation. Sometimes the starting number is recorded wrong.
Wrong how? By the man who installed it?
It can happen, yes. Either the final read on the old meter or the starting read on the new one gets entered incorrectly. I can't say that's what happened here, but it's the first thing to check.
Well, somebody should check it. This is the second time I call about something with this city and I am tired of explaining.
I understand. I'll put the details in the note so you won't have to start over. Can I confirm a callback number?
Four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-six-seven.
Got it. Zero one six seven. Someone from the meter team will call you, and you can have that plumber's receipt ready to read the date to them.
I will. Now, another question. If I have to pay it while you check, can I pay on a Saturday or Sunday? I am not able to drive downtown easily in the week, and I do not want a penalty.
There's a payment drop box at City Hall that's available outside regular hours, so you could use it over the weekend with a check. You can also pay online any time of day, including weekends.
Online. I do not like that so much. But my niece can help. Is there a phone line on Sunday?
I don't believe the office is staffed on weekends, so the drop box or the online site would be the way to go. If you'd like, I can note that you're disputing the bill so it's documented.

Yes, please note it. Dispute. Put that. I am looking out the window right now, actually. I am parked at the beach lot, I came to get my prescription nearby, and the water looks flat from here. Very calm. Nothing unusual. I say this because I do not understand where so much water could go.
Fair point, and I'll include that you've had no unusual usage. Is there anything else I can look at for you today?
No. Just have someone call me. I have been patient, but this is a lot of money for a woman on a pension.
Understood, Ms. Sullivan. The note is in, and the meter team will be in touch. Thank you for calling.
Thank you. Goodbye.
